curriculum: Appendix E confirms an English-taught 180 EC bachelor: ten 7.5 EC foundation courses, a mandatory 15 EC project, 45 EC of major-bound electives including 30 EC at level 3 and 45 EC free elective space. No formal route is required. The student page describes the four profiles as frameworks for selecting electives. The previous example fixed six selections without establishing their combined entry and scheduling conditions. Current rules instead support preserving the genuine choice blocks. Appendix E excludes overlapping coursework and flags individual courses requiring approval or no longer offered.
progression: The overview schedules seven level-1 foundations and three level-2 foundations. The published first-year binding study advice threshold is 45 EC. The major elective rules require the applicable Osiris prerequisites, mandatory-course priority and one elective per time slot, subject to approved exceptions and availability. The thesis requires 120 EC and completion of all mandatory foundation courses. The project guidance allows laboratory or computational research and describes an individual project, written thesis and presentation. The erratum adds Mathematics, Data & Molecular Modelling; the separate NMR Spectroscopy and Molecular Modelling elective ended after 2025–2026.
components: Physical Chemistry for the Life Sciences
Choose six approved courses, with at least 30 EC at advanced level.
Start after passing the foundation courses and earning at least 120 EC. The project can involve laboratory or computational research.
